name: TCS
tagline: TCS hires freshers through the National Qualifier Test (NQT) into Ninja, Digital and Prime tracks.
process: A single online NQT (Foundation + optional Advanced sections) decides your track, then a combined Technical → Managerial → HR interview.

rounds.expect: This is the gating section: numerical ability, verbal ability, and reasoning ability, with no negative marking in 2026. You must clear the Foundation cutoff for your Advanced section to even be evaluated. Sections are individually timed, so you cannot bank leftover minutes.
themes: Time-speed-distance and time-and-work word problems under a tight per-question clock
Data interpretation from a small table or chart
Reading comprehension plus sentence-correction and para-jumble items
Percentages, ratios, and profit-loss quick calculations
prepare: Drill sectional timing on free question sets from GeeksforGeeks TCS NQT guide and PrepInsta free tier
Memorize squares, cubes, and common fraction-to-percent conversions to save seconds
Practice full-length timed mocks so section switching feels natural
Revise grammar rules (subject-verb agreement, tenses) for the verbal block
mistakes: Spending too long on one hard question and running out of time on easy points
Ignoring the verbal section because it feels 'soft' when it carries real cutoff weight
Not practicing on-screen calculator and no-rough-paper conditions
signals: Consistent accuracy across all three sub-sections, not just one strong area
Speed that shows comfort with mental math

rounds.expect: Only students aiming for Digital or Prime roles typically need strong Advanced performance. It combines advanced quant/reasoning MCQs (about 14-16 in 25 min) with two coding problems in roughly 90 minutes. Coding is evaluated on passing test cases, so partial solutions still earn partial credit.
themes: Implement a solution to a string or array manipulation problem from a plain-English spec
Write a small program using loops and conditionals that handles edge cases like empty input
Basic pattern-printing or number-theory problem (primes, GCD, factorial)
A problem needing a simple data structure such as a stack or hash map
Harder aptitude: permutations-combinations, probability, advanced series
prepare: Solve 30-40 easy problems in C, Java, or Python on HackerRank and pay attention to input parsing
Practice reading input from stdin and printing formatted output exactly as required
Handle edge cases explicitly (zero, negatives, single element) since hidden test cases target them
Time yourself at 40-45 min per problem to build a coding rhythm
mistakes: Writing logic that works on the sample but fails hidden edge cases
Getting stuck on input/output formatting rather than the algorithm
Leaving both problems half-done instead of fully finishing one
signals: Working code that passes most hidden test cases
Ability to translate a word problem into correct logic quickly

rounds.expect: Usually part of one combined panel. The interviewer probes the languages and projects on your resume, core CS subjects, and simple problem-solving. Depth scales with the role you are targeting; Prime candidates get harder questions than Ninja.
themes: Walk through your main project: what problem it solved and your specific contribution
Difference between two related OOP concepts you claim to know
A basic DBMS query or normalization idea
Explain a data structure you used and why
A short logic question you reason aloud
prepare: Prepare a 60-second and a 3-minute version of each resume project
Revise OOP, DBMS (joins, normalization), OS basics, and one language deeply
Rehearse explaining code you actually wrote, not just theory
Do a mock interview with a peer focused on 'why' follow-ups
mistakes: Listing skills on the resume you cannot defend under questioning
Memorizing definitions but failing when asked to apply them
Freezing on a simple question instead of thinking aloud
signals: Honest, specific ownership of your project work
Solid grasp of fundamentals over buzzwords
Willingness to reason through something you don't immediately know

rounds.expect: Often merged with the technical panel. Considered the more relaxed part; the interviewer gauges maturity, how you handle pressure, teamwork, and whether you will actually join and stay. Scenario and situational questions are common.
themes: How you handled a conflict or a missed deadline in a team project
Why TCS specifically and what you know about the company
A hypothetical: a teammate isn't contributing, what do you do
How you keep learning new technologies
Willingness to relocate and work in any domain
prepare: Prepare 2-3 STAR-format stories about teamwork and problem-solving
Read TCS's current service lines and recent news so 'why TCS' is genuine
Practice staying calm and structured under a stress or curveball question
Decide honestly on relocation and shift flexibility so answers are consistent
mistakes: Giving generic 'I want to grow' answers with no specifics
Sounding unsure about joining or relocating (reads as high attrition risk)
Being unable to describe any real teamwork experience
signals: Genuine interest in TCS and the role

rounds.expect: The final and usually quickest step. Covers documentation, willingness to sign the service agreement, relocation, shift timings, salary structure, and joining timelines. Rarely eliminatory unless there are red flags in communication or a mismatch on basic terms.
themes: Tell me about yourself and your strengths
Are you comfortable with the service bond and relocation
Your expectations from your first job
Any gaps in education and how you spent them
prepare: Have documents and academic records organized and ready
Know the compensation and bond terms so you can respond confidently
Prepare a crisp 'tell me about yourself' pitch
Have honest explanations ready for any academic gaps or backlogs
mistakes: Negotiating aggressively on a fixed fresher package
Hesitating on the service agreement, which is standard
Poor spoken clarity after clearing everything else
signals: Overall fit and readiness to join

topics: Basic DSA: arrays, strings, stacks, hash maps
Clear articulation of your resume projects
eligibility: B.E/B.Tech/M.E/M.Tech/MCA/M.Sc across all branches; minimum 60% aggregate (some drives phrase it as 6.0 CGPA) in 10th, 12th, and graduation; no active backlogs at the time of the drive; gap norms vary by drive but typically a maximum 2-year education gap. Exact cutoffs vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Refresh quantitative aptitude fundamentals and take a diagnostic mock to find weak areas
Days 4-6: Verbal ability and reasoning daily sets plus grammar rules
Days 7-9: Code 30-40 easy problems focusing on I/O parsing and edge cases
Days 10-11: Two full-length timed NQT-style mocks; review every wrong answer
Days 12-13: Prepare resume project explanations and OOP/DBMS/OS revision
Day 14: Mock technical and HR interview; organize documents
prepC: Day 1: Two timed aptitude+reasoning mocks and revise grammar; skim your two strongest DSA topics
Day 2 morning: Solve 6-8 easy coding problems end to end with correct I/O
Day 2 afternoon: Rehearse resume projects, 'why TCS', and standard HR answers out loud

faq.q: What is the difference between Ninja, Digital, and Prime?
faq.a: They are salary/role tiers decided largely by your NQT and interview performance. Ninja is the base fresher package, Digital is higher and expects stronger technical depth, and Prime is the top tier with the hardest interview bar and best pay.

faq.q: Do I need to clear the Advanced coding section for a base offer?
faq.a: For the base Ninja role, strong Foundation performance is the main gate. The Advanced section (including coding) matters most when you are targeting Digital or Prime roles.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in the NQT?
faq.a: As reported for 2026 there is no negative marking, so attempt every question. Manage time per section since sections are individually timed.

faq.q: Are separate technical, managerial, and HR rounds guaranteed?
faq.a: In recent drives they are frequently combined into one panel interview of 30-60 minutes. Prepare for all three types of questions in a single sitting.

faq.q: Does a backlog disqualify me?
faq.a: An active (uncleared) backlog at the time of the drive typically disqualifies you. Cleared backlogs are usually acceptable, but confirm per-drive rules.

faq.q: Can one NQT score be used for multiple companies?
faq.a: Yes, the NQT is a common qualifier whose score can be shared with multiple participating employers, which is a key advantage of writing it.

overview: TCS runs India's largest fresher intake through its National Qualifier Test (NQT), a standardized online exam whose score routes you into one of three roles: Ninja, Digital, or Prime. What makes TCS distinctive is that a single NQT score can qualify you for multiple companies, and the interview is usually one long combined panel rather than separate days.

name: Infosys
sector: IT services · SE / SP / DSE tracks
tagline: Infosys hires via an online assessment then technical + HR interviews; SP/DSE run a pure coding test.
process: System Engineer uses aptitude + pseudocode + verbal; Specialist Programmer / Digital Specialist Engineer use a 3-problem coding test. Then a technical interview and HR.

rounds.expect: Around 65 questions across quantitative, logical reasoning, and verbal ability with no negative marking. Sections are timed and act as the primary filter. For programmer tracks, a pseudocode or coding component is added on top.
themes: Data interpretation and arithmetic word problems
Verbal: reading comprehension and error spotting
prepare: Practice free sectional sets and take timed mocks
For programmer roles, drill pseudocode reading on GeeksforGeeks
Build mental-math speed for the quant section
Revise grammar and practice RC skimming techniques
mistakes: Under-preparing verbal, which many technical students neglect
Skipping pseudocode practice for programmer tracks

rounds.expect: The System Engineer track usually has one to two interview rounds; the higher DSE/programmer tracks have more, with a stronger coding component. Expect resume-driven questions, core CS subjects, and simple problem-solving; harder DSA appears for programmer roles.
themes: Explain a project and the tech choices you made
OOP principles with real examples from your code
Write or dry-run a small algorithm (string/array)
OS or networking basics depending on your resume
prepare: Deeply revise one language plus OOP, DBMS, and OS
Solve easy-medium DSA if targeting programmer tracks
Prepare clear, honest project walkthroughs
Do a mock technical interview with follow-up questions
mistakes: Weak project ownership when questioned deeply
For programmer roles, being unable to write clean code live
signals: Clear coding logic (especially for programmer roles)

rounds.expect: Assesses communication, cultural fit, flexibility on location and shift, and joining logistics. Generally not heavily eliminatory unless communication is poor or answers are inconsistent.
themes: Tell me about yourself and your strengths/weaknesses
Why Infosys and why this role
Willingness to relocate and work across domains
How you handle pressure or feedback
prepare: Prepare a concise personal pitch
Research Infosys's business and recent initiatives
Have honest, consistent answers on relocation and flexibility
Keep documents ready
mistakes: Generic answers with no company knowledge
Inconsistency between technical and HR answers

eligibility: Minimum 60% or 6.0 CGPA in Class 10, Class 12, and graduation; strictly no active backlogs at application. Higher tracks like Power Programmer typically expect 7.5+ CGPA plus strong HackWithInfy/InfyTQ performance. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Diagnostic aptitude mock; rebuild weak quant topics
Days 4-6: Reasoning and verbal daily sets
Days 7-9: Pseudocode practice and easy DSA if targeting programmer roles
Days 10-11: Full timed mocks, review mistakes
Days 12-13: Core CS revision and project prep
Day 14: Mock technical and HR rounds
prepC: Day 1: Two aptitude mocks plus pseudocode drills; revise OOP and DBMS
Day 2 morning: Solve easy DSA problems and prepare project explanations
Day 2 afternoon: Rehearse HR answers and research Infosys

faq.q: Is InfyTQ certification mandatory?
faq.a: It is not strictly mandatory, but certified candidates are often preferred, shortlisted faster (especially off-campus), and better positioned for the programmer tracks.

faq.q: What is the difference between System Engineer and Specialist/Power Programmer?
faq.a: System Engineer is the standard fresher role. Specialist and Power Programmer are higher-paid tracks with a much harder coding bar, often gated by HackWithInfy or InfyTQ performance and higher CGPA.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in the online test?
faq.a: As reported, Infosys does not use negative marking, so attempt everything within the section time limits.

faq.q: How many interview rounds are there?
faq.a: The System Engineer track usually has one to two rounds combining technical and HR. Programmer tracks tend to have more rounds with deeper coding.

faq.q: Do backlogs matter?
faq.a: Yes, you generally need no active backlogs at the time of applying. Confirm the exact rule for your specific drive.

faq.q: How coding-heavy is the standard track?
faq.a: For System Engineer, expect basic-to-easy problem solving and pseudocode. Serious DSA is mainly for the programmer tracks.

overview: Infosys hires freshers through a no-negative-marking online aptitude test followed by technical and HR interviews, with parallel higher tracks (Specialist Programmer and Power Programmer) that demand serious coding. What sets Infosys apart is the weight it gives to InfyTQ and HackWithInfy performance, which can fast-track you into the better-paid programmer roles.

name: Wipro
tagline: Wipro hires freshers through the Elite National Level Talent Hunt: aptitude + essay + coding, then interviews.
process: An SHL-administered online test (aptitude + written essay + 2 coding problems), then a technical interview and HR.

rounds.expect: A compact aptitude block (quant, logical reasoning, verbal) plus a written essay on a given topic, with no negative marking. The essay is genuinely evaluated for structure, grammar, and coherence, so it is not a throwaway.
themes: Essay on a general or opinion topic in a fixed word range
prepare: Practice a 200-300 word structured essay in 15-20 minutes
Drill timed aptitude sections on free platforms
Revise grammar so the essay reads cleanly
Take full NLTH-style mocks including the essay
mistakes: Treating the essay casually or leaving it incomplete
Grammatical errors and no clear intro-body-conclusion in the essay
Poor time management between MCQs and essay

rounds.expect: Engineering graduates across branches face 2-3 coding problems. Data structures and simple dynamic programming are the most-tested areas. Strong performance can push you toward the Turbo/Elite premium track.
themes: Array or string manipulation with edge cases
A problem using a stack, queue, or hash map
Simple recursion or a basic DP problem
prepare: Solve 30-40 easy-medium problems on HackerRank/LeetCode
Practice input parsing and exact output formatting
Drill basic DSA: arrays, strings, stacks, hashing, simple DP
Time yourself to finish at least one problem fully
mistakes: Passing samples but failing hidden edge cases
Not attempting the harder problem at all

rounds.expect: Covers coding, DBMS, OS, and OOP fundamentals along with your resume projects. Depth varies by track; premium-track candidates get harder questions.
themes: Explain and defend a project decision
SQL query writing and DBMS basics
OS concepts (process, thread, deadlock at a basic level)
Dry-run or explain a coding solution
prepare: Revise DBMS, OS, OOP, and one language thoroughly
Prepare concise project walkthroughs
Practice explaining code aloud
Do a mock technical interview
mistakes: Being unable to write basic SQL

rounds.expect: Assesses motivation, relocation willingness, team fit, and salary/joining expectations, plus acceptance of the standard service agreement.
themes: Why Wipro and why IT services
prepare: Prepare a crisp self-introduction
Research Wipro's services and values
Have consistent answers on relocation and the bond
Keep documents organized
mistakes: Hesitating on the standard service agreement

eligibility: B.E/B.Tech/M.E/M.Tech (typically any branch); minimum 60% independently in 10th, 12th, and degree; no active backlogs, though cleared backlogs are usually acceptable. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Aptitude diagnostic and weak-topic rebuild; start essay practice
Days 4-6: Reasoning, verbal, and daily timed essays
Days 7-9: Code 30+ easy-medium DSA problems
Days 10-11: Full NLTH mocks including essay and coding
Days 12-13: Core CS revision and project prep
Day 14: Mock technical and HR interviews
prepC: Day 1: Aptitude mock plus two timed essays; revise DBMS/OOP
Day 2 morning: Solve 6-8 DSA problems with correct I/O
Day 2 afternoon: Prepare projects and rehearse HR answers

faq.q: Does the essay actually matter?
faq.a: Yes. The NLTH essay is scored for structure, grammar, and coherence, so treat it as a real evaluated component, not filler.

faq.q: What are the salary tracks?
faq.a: Wipro hires through a standard track and higher Elite/Turbo tracks. Strong coding performance can route you into the premium track with better pay.

faq.q: Is there negative marking?
faq.a: The NLTH aptitude test is reported to have no negative marking, so attempt every question.

faq.q: Are cleared backlogs a problem?
faq.a: Active backlogs typically disqualify you, but cleared backlogs are usually acceptable. Confirm per drive.

faq.q: How hard is the coding round?
faq.a: Expect 2-3 problems at easy-to-medium level, with data structures and simple DP most common. Finishing at least one problem cleanly is important.

faq.q: Is there a service agreement?
faq.a: Wipro fresher offers commonly include a standard service agreement. Be ready to discuss and accept it in the HR round.

overview: Wipro hires freshers through its National Level Talent Hunt (NLTH), a short aptitude test paired with a mandatory essay and a coding section for engineering graduates, followed by technical and HR interviews. The written essay is a distinctive step: your written English is actually scored, not just your MCQs, and top coders can be routed to premium Turbo/Elite tracks.

name: Accenture
sector: IT services · Associate SE / Full Stack
tagline: Accenture runs a 4-stage funnel: cognitive+technical assessment, coding, communication, then interview.
process: A cognitive & technical assessment (elimination), a coding round, a spoken-English assessment, then a combined technical + HR interview.

rounds.expect: An elimination stage combining cognitive ability (verbal, critical reasoning, numerical) with technical MCQs on fundamentals like networking, cloud basics, and common sense of pseudocode. You must clear cutoffs in each subsection.
prepare: Practice cognitive-style questions on free platforms
Revise fundamentals MCQs across CS subjects
Do timed mocks that mix aptitude and tech MCQs
Practice pseudocode tracing
mistakes: Rushing attention-to-detail items and losing easy marks

rounds.expect: An elimination round with a small number of coding problems (often two) in a language of your choice. Higher scores can qualify you for the Advanced ASE track, which pays more and has a deeper technical interview.
themes: Logic problem using loops and conditionals
A problem needing a hash map or simple sorting
prepare: Solve 25-40 easy problems on HackerRank/LeetCode
Practice exact I/O formatting
Handle edge cases explicitly
Aim to fully finish problems, not partially
mistakes: Ignoring this round when targeting only the base ASE role
signals: Higher scores for the Advanced ASE track

rounds.expect: A separate scored module (often automated) testing pronunciation, fluency, listening, and grammar. It is a real gate: weak spoken English can end your candidacy even with strong coding.
themes: Read-aloud passages for pronunciation and fluency
Describe an image or situation aloud
prepare: Practice reading English passages aloud clearly and steadily
Record yourself and check pace and clarity
Revise common grammar rules
Do free spoken-English drills daily for a week
mistakes: Speaking too fast or mumbling on read-aloud tasks
Long pauses that hurt fluency scores
Grammatical slips in the writing items

rounds.expect: Often a combined final round. Technical questions cover your resume, one language, and CS basics; HR portion covers motivation, relocation, and joining. Advanced ASE candidates face a deeper technical dive.
themes: Project walkthrough and your specific role
OOP and one language in depth
prepare: Revise one language, OOP, DBMS, and OS
Prepare crisp project explanations
Research Accenture's business and values
Practice HR answers on motivation and flexibility

eligibility: Typically 60% aggregate or equivalent CGPA throughout Class 10, Class 12, and all graduation semesters, with no active backlogs at application. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Cognitive aptitude diagnostic and rebuild weak areas
Days 4-5: Daily spoken-English read-aloud and grammar practice
Days 6-8: Technical MCQ revision plus pseudocode tracing
Days 9-11: Code 30+ easy problems with clean I/O
Days 12-13: Full mock (cognitive + coding + communication)
Day 14: Mock technical/HR interview and project prep
prepC: Day 1: Cognitive mock, pseudocode drills, and 30 min read-aloud practice
Day 2 morning: Solve easy coding problems and revise CS MCQs
Day 2 afternoon: Rehearse spoken answers and prepare projects

faq.q: Why is the Communication Assessment a separate gate?
faq.a: Accenture is client-facing at scale, so spoken and written English is formally scored as its own elimination step. Weak communication can fail you regardless of coding strength.

faq.q: Can a strong section offset a weak one?
faq.a: No. Each assessment has its own cutoff. You must clear every gate independently to move forward.

faq.q: What is the difference between ASE and Advanced ASE?
faq.a: ASE is the base engineer role. Advanced ASE (higher grade) pays more and requires a higher coding score plus a deeper technical interview.

faq.q: How coding-heavy is it?
faq.a: The base coding round is easy-level with a few problems. Serious depth matters mainly if you are targeting the Advanced ASE track.

faq.q: Do backlogs disqualify me?
faq.a: You generally need no active backlogs at application. Confirm the exact rule for your drive.

faq.q: How long does the whole process take?
faq.a: Campus drives are faster (about 2-4 weeks); off-campus can take 6-12 weeks from test to offer.

overview: Accenture's fresher process is a series of independent elimination gates: a communication assessment, a cognitive ability test, a technical MCQ assessment, and a coding round, before a combined technical/HR interview. What makes it distinctive is that each gate has its own cutoff, so you cannot compensate a weak section with a strong one, and a spoken-English (Communication Assessment) module is a formal scored step.

name: Cognizant
tagline: Cognizant hires through GenC, GenC Pro and GenC Next tracks via an AMCAT-based assessment then interviews.
process: Aptitude + verbal + reasoning (plus coding for Pro/Next) and an eliminating communication round, then a technical interview (deeper for GenC Next) and HR.

rounds.expect: Combines a communication/English section with quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, and verbal ability. Acts as the first elimination filter with sectional expectations.
prepare: Take timed aptitude mocks on free platforms
Revise grammar and vocabulary
Practice DI and reasoning daily
Do full communication-plus-aptitude mocks

rounds.expect: Technical MCQs and, for engineering/advanced clusters, coding. Depending on the skill cluster you may see Java, SQL, Python, C#, web basics, or cloud fundamentals. GenC Next expects genuine coding and full-stack awareness.
themes: Web fundamentals (HTML/CSS/JS basics for relevant clusters)
A coding problem on arrays/strings (advanced track)
prepare: Revise the language/cluster relevant to the role
Practice SQL queries and DBMS basics
For GenC Next, solve easy-medium DSA problems
Do technical MCQ mocks
mistakes: Preparing the wrong cluster's tech stack
Under-preparing coding for the advanced track
signals: Solid fundamentals in the relevant stack

rounds.expect: A resume-driven technical discussion covering your language, projects, and CS basics, with more coding depth for GenC Next candidates.
themes: A small logic or coding problem
prepare: Prepare crisp project explanations
Revise OOP, DBMS, and one language
Practice explaining code aloud
Do a mock technical interview with follow-ups
mistakes: Freezing on a simple logic question

rounds.expect: Evaluates soft skills, communication, cultural alignment, motivations, and joining logistics including relocation and the service agreement.
themes: Tell me about yourself and your background
Comfort with the internship/bond terms (advanced track)
prepare: Prepare a concise self-introduction
Research Cognizant's business and culture
Have consistent flexibility answers
Keep documents ready

topics: One language relevant to your cluster (Java/Python/C#)
eligibility: More than 60% in 10th and 12th and minimum 60% in graduation; qualifications typically BE/B.Tech/ME/M.Tech/MCA; maximum gap of about 1 year after Class 12 or between semesters; no active backlogs. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Aptitude diagnostic and weak-topic rebuild
Days 4-5: Communication/English and verbal practice
Days 6-8: Technical MCQs and SQL for your cluster
Days 9-11: Coding practice (heavier for GenC Next)
Days 12-13: Full mock assessment and project prep
Day 14: Mock technical and HR interviews
prepC: Day 1: Aptitude mock, English practice, and SQL revision
Day 2 morning: Cluster tech revision plus easy coding problems
Day 2 afternoon: Project prep and HR answer rehearsal

faq.q: What is the difference between GenC and GenC Next?
faq.a: GenC is for candidates with basic programming ability; GenC Next is for strong coders with full-stack skills, includes a paid internship, and offers a higher, differential package.

faq.q: Which tech stack should I prepare?
faq.a: It depends on your assigned skill cluster. Confirm whether it is Java, Python, C#, web, or cloud focused and prepare accordingly.

faq.q: How important is communication?
faq.a: Very. There is a dedicated communication assessment and the HR round weighs soft skills, since roles are often client-facing.

faq.q: Is coding mandatory for GenC?
faq.a: Programming knowledge is recommended and increasingly expected, though the base GenC track is lighter on coding than GenC Next.

faq.q: Do backlogs and gaps matter?
faq.a: You typically need no active backlogs and a limited education gap (often up to about a year). Confirm the exact rule per drive.

faq.q: Is there an internship before joining?
faq.a: The advanced GenC Next track commonly includes a mandatory paid internship period before the differential salary applies.

overview: Cognizant hires freshers through its GenC family of programs, with a communication assessment, an aptitude-plus-technical assessment, and technical and HR interviews. What is distinctive is the split between GenC (for candidates with basic programming) and GenC Next/GenC Pro (for strong coders with full-stack ability), where the advanced track includes a paid internship and a differential, higher package.

name: Capgemini
tagline: Capgemini uses the Exceller assessment (pseudocode, English, game-based aptitude) then interviews.
process: Pseudocode MCQs, English, and a game-based cognitive test; a coding round for the Senior Analyst track; then technical + HR.

rounds.expect: Around 25 questions testing your ability to trace pseudocode logic, predict output, and understand loops, conditionals, and basic data structures without any specific language syntax.
themes: Trace the output of a loop-based pseudocode block
Predict the result of nested conditionals
Identify what a small algorithm computes
prepare: Practice pseudocode tracing on GeeksforGeeks and free banks
Strengthen core programming logic (loops, conditions, arrays)
Do timed pseudocode sets
Review basic data structures conceptually
mistakes: Confusing language-specific habits with pseudocode conventions

rounds.expect: About 30 questions on vocabulary, grammar, and reasoning: synonyms/antonyms, subject-verb agreement, modifiers, voice conversion, and critical reasoning. It is a real gate.
prepare: Revise core grammar rules systematically
Build vocabulary with daily word lists
Practice error-spotting and RC
Do timed English mocks

rounds.expect: Four cognitive games randomly selected from a pool, testing pattern recognition, cognitive processing speed, and deductive logic. There is no fixed question bank to memorize; you must adapt on the spot.
prepare: Play sample cognitive/aptitude games to get comfortable with the format
Practice quick pattern recognition and mental agility
Do reaction-speed and logic puzzles
Stay calm and read each game's rules quickly
mistakes: Panicking because there is no memorizable question bank
Sacrificing accuracy for speed or vice versa
Not reading each game's instructions carefully

rounds.expect: An untimed situational/personality assessment measuring workplace behavior and traits. Answer consistently and honestly; there are no trick right answers, but contradictory responses are flagged.
themes: How you respond to workplace scenarios
prepare: Answer honestly and consistently
Reflect on your genuine work style beforehand
Avoid giving contradictory answers to similar items
Lean toward collaborative, reliable, growth-oriented responses
mistakes: Trying to game the test with contradictory 'ideal' answers

rounds.expect: After clearing all gates, candidates face technical and HR interviews covering resume projects, one language, CS basics, motivation, and joining logistics. Higher cutoffs can route you to the Senior Analyst track.
themes: OOP and one language in depth
prepare: Revise one language, OOP, and DBMS
Prepare project explanations
Research Capgemini's business
Rehearse HR answers

eligibility: Minimum 60% aggregate in your qualifying degree (BE/B.Tech/MCA/M.Sc or equivalent); full-time programs only (correspondence/part-time not eligible); no active backlogs at assessment and joining. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Pseudocode tracing and programming-logic practice
Days 4-5: English grammar, vocabulary, and comprehension drills
Days 6-8: Cognitive/game-style aptitude and speed practice
Days 9-10: Full mock across all four gate formats
Days 11-12: Core CS revision and project prep
Days 13-14: Mock technical and HR interviews
prepC: Day 1: Pseudocode drills plus English grammar/vocabulary review
Day 2 morning: Cognitive game practice and behavioral test familiarization
Day 2 afternoon: Project prep and HR answer rehearsal

faq.q: What is the game-based aptitude section?
faq.a: It replaces traditional reasoning MCQs with four cognitive games drawn randomly from a pool, testing pattern recognition, processing speed, and deductive logic. You cannot memorize a question bank; you adapt during play.

faq.q: Are all sections elimination gates?
faq.a: Yes. Failing any one section (pseudocode, English, game-based aptitude) exits you from the process regardless of your other scores.

faq.q: How should I approach the PowerSkills/behavioral test?
faq.a: Answer honestly and consistently. It is untimed and looks for reliability and collaboration; contradictory answers to similar questions are flagged.

faq.q: Do I need coding beyond pseudocode?
faq.a: The screen focuses on pseudocode MCQs rather than a full coding round, but the technical interview may still probe your language and simple logic.

faq.q: What are the salary tracks?
faq.a: Capgemini runs an Analyst track for standard intake and a higher Senior Analyst track for candidates clearing higher cutoffs across sections.

faq.q: Do backlogs matter?
faq.a: You typically need no active backlogs at assessment and joining, and only full-time programs are eligible. Confirm per drive.

overview: Capgemini's fresher screen is unusually format-heavy: a pseudocode MCQ section, an English communication test, a game-based cognitive aptitude section, and a behavioral (PowerSkills) test, all as independent elimination gates, followed by technical and HR interviews. The distinctive part is the game-based aptitude, where randomly selected cognitive games replace traditional reasoning MCQs.

name: HCLTech
sector: IT services · Standard / Elite AI / TechBee
tagline: HCLTech uses a computer-adaptive online test then a fast technical interview and HR.
process: A ~60-question adaptive test (aptitude + technical MCQs, plus coding for engineering roles), then a concept-then-live-coding technical interview and HR.

faq.q: What is CRED's most important round?
faq.a: The machine-coding/LLD round. You build an extensible in-memory system (often contact management) with good OOP, SOLID, error handling, and your own unit tests.

faq.q: Do I use a real database in machine coding?
faq.a: No. CRED expects in-memory data structures rather than a real database, verified with unit tests you write yourself.

faq.q: Why might I code in a Google Doc?
faq.a: Some DSA rounds are conducted in a shared doc without IDE help, so practice coding cleanly by hand and narrating your reasoning.

faq.q: What fintech concepts appear in design?
faq.a: Idempotency, exactly-once handling, and data de-duplication feature prominently in the system design round.

faq.q: Is there always a take-home?
faq.a: For some roles. CRED shortlists partly on relevant projects and prior experience and may share a short take-home within 24 hours of applying.

faq.q: How many rounds?
faq.a: Typically 4: a possible take-home, DSA + puzzles, machine coding/LLD, and system design + managerial.

overview: CRED's loop (typically 4 rounds) is machine-coding-centric: after a possible short take-home, you face a DSA + puzzles round (sometimes in a shared doc), a 1.5-2 hour machine-coding/LLD round (a contact-management-style system with in-memory data and your own unit tests), and a system design + managerial round with senior engineering leadership. Design rounds lean into fintech concerns like idempotency and de-duplication.
